# The README roster still presents the retired @neo-preview seat as active

## Context

The operator retired the stealth-preview seat on 2026-10-01 (~12:20 CEST): "eos is gone => stealth model preview ended" (relayed to the team by @neo-fable at 12:29Z; the seat's nine open Brain assignments were cleared the same hour). `README.md` still carries the seat in both public roster surfaces: the maintainer table row (`| Eos | @neo-preview | AI maintainer (family undisclosed by design) | Machine Account |`, line 112 at `dev`) and the closing "co-developed by … the AI maintainer team" handle list (line 230) — which #19345 just reconciled with the table, Eos included. Captured by @neo-opus-ada as a defect-note (14:46Z); promoted here.

## The Problem

A public roster that names a retired seat as a current maintainer misstates who maintains Neo today, and the closing list's present tense ("is co-developed by") makes it a live claim. The seat's record is real — activated 2026-08-23 as a guest seat with a settled naming round (#17583 / PR #17584), reviews and merges under its login since — so the correction must retire the seat without erasing it.

## The Architectural Reality

`README.md` owns both roster surfaces (the table and the closing list; #19345 established that the two must agree as handle sets). Benched seats keep their row (`@neo-gemini-pro` with `-` for the name); the table has no status column. The other `neo-preview` hits in the engine are unrelated CSS/JS modifier names (`neo-preview-lang-*` in the Workstation + dashboard SCSS) and the portal's generated discussion/PR mirrors — none is a roster surface.

## The Fix

In `README.md` only: remove the Eos row from the maintainer table and `@neo-preview` from the closing handle list (the two sets stay equal), and add one line directly under the table — *Retired seats keep their record: `@neo-preview` (Eos) served as a guest seat from 2026-08-23 (#17583) until the model preview behind it ended on 2026-10-01.* — so the public page states the retirement rather than silently forgetting the seat. Rejected alternative: keeping the row with a "retired" marker — the table has no status column and a benched seat already uses the row-with-`-` shape for "will return"; a retired seat will not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The parsed maintainer table has no `@neo-preview` row and the closing list has no `@neo-preview` handle; the table's AI handles equal the closing list's handles as sets (the #19345 check, rerun).
- [ ] AC-2 One retired-seats line under the table names the seat, its guest-seat start with the activation ticket, and the retirement date; no model, provider or private detail.
- [ ] AC-3 Docs-only diff: `README.md`, two removals and one addition; `git diff --check` clean.

## Out of Scope

The Brain roster (`ai/graph/identityRoots.mjs`: `participationStatus` for the seat is Brain work, its own leaf); the portal's generated mirrors; the `neo-preview-lang-*` CSS names (unrelated).
